title: The Art of Staying Ahead of Deadlines: Improved Algorithms for the Minimum Tardy Processing Time

The original arXiv paper (2402.16847v1) has a full 11-entry bibliography. The central reference [5] (Fischer & Wennmann, arXiv:2402.13357), on which the entire algorithm depends, is absent.

The summation runs over i ∈ [n], but the summand |\widetilde{S}_j \setminus S_{j-1}| depends only on j — the index i does not appear in the summand. As written, the LHS equals n·|\widetilde{S}_j \setminus S_{j-1}| and the bound fails whenever the difference set is nonempty and n ≥ 2. The intended statement is ∑_{j ∈ [n]} |\widetilde{S}_j \setminus S_{j-1}| ≤ d_max + 1, mirroring Lemma 4.1 which correctly uses j as the summation index. The same i/j mismatch propagates through the entire proof (EQUATION::0, EQUATION::1, PROOF::0). The verifier confirmed the original source paper (arXiv 2402.16847) was withdrawn by the author because the runtime analysis in Section 3 is incorrect.

summary: The paper proposes an Õ(n + d_max)-time algorithm for the 1‖∑pjUj scheduling problem by refining Fischer and Wennmann's approach. Verification across four specialist verifiers (math, text, citation, cross-section consistency) in exhaustive/lenient mode identified 9 issues, including 5 high-confidence errors (≥0.85). The most critical findings are: (1) references [1]-[8] are cited throughout but missing from the bibliography, including the central Fischer & Wennmann [5] reference the entire paper builds upon (confidence 1.0); (2) Lemma 3.2 has a summation index mismatch (∑_{i ∈ [n]} of a j-indexed summand) that invalidates the stated bound as written — the arXiv version of this paper was withdrawn by the author due to an incorrect runtime analysis in Section 3 (confidence 0.97); (3) equations (3a)-(3c) are referenced three times but never defined in the text (confidence 0.95); (4) an undefined variable J is used in the Earliest-Deadline-First feasibility condition (confidence 0.90); (5) S_j is used where S_{j-1} is intended in the algorithm description (confidence 0.90). Additional lower-confidence issues include notation inconsistencies and an under-analyzed multi-machine runtime claim. The paper's cited references [9], [10], [11] were verified as real and accurately described. The combination of high-confidence errors — particularly the missing central reference, the index error known to have caused the author's withdrawal, and the missing equation definitions — warrants correction before publication.
